anomalies.observed: On the regulator sheet, U1 (LM1117-5.0) has its input pin VI (U1.2) tied to the +5V net (the same net that C2 decouples and that the VO pin U1.3 is also tied to). anomalies.expected: For an LM1117-5.0 used to generate the +5V rail, VIN (U1.2) must be connected to the unregulated input rail (VCC from J5), and VOUT (U1.3) to the regulated +5V net. VIN and VOUT must not be on the same net.

evidence.quote: U1 LM1117-5.0: pin 2 'VI' wire runs to '+5V' (with C2 100nF); pin 3 'VO' wire also runs to '+5V'
J5 PWR pin 2 -> VCC (separate net from +5V, joined only via JP1 VCC_STABLE)

anomalies.impact: The 5 V regulator cannot regulate the raw VCC supply: with VIN shorted to VOUT the part does nothing, so the +5 V rail (which powers both ATtiny MCUs) exists only if the VCC_STABLE jumper JP1 is closed, directly shorting VCC to +5 V and bypassing the regulator entirely (and placing the input decoupling cap C2 on the wrong side).

anomalies.observed: R1 is drawn with value '10' (10 ohm) connecting VCC to the VCC_OUT node (the drain of the high-side PMOS Q1), i.e. in parallel with the Q1 channel.
anomalies.expected: A resistor bridging the switched supply to the fan rail in this position should be a high-value gate/bleed resistor (or be omitted); a 10-ohm parallel path defeats the high-side switch.

evidence.quote: R1 value '10' between VCC and the Q1/Q2/VCC_OUT node, while every other resistor is 1K/10K

anomalies.impact: A 10-ohm path from VCC to VCC_OUT keeps the fan partially powered when Q1 is off (fan cannot fully stop) and, if Q2 is driven, sinks ~0.5 A through R1/Q2.
